# Descriptive analysis {background-color='{{< brand color blue >}}' .bkg-buildings}

## Common workflow {.bkg-trees}

::: {.incremental}

1. Create a `tbl_svy` object (a survey object) using `as_survey_design()` or `as_survey_rep()`

2. Subset data (if needed) using `filter()` (to create subpopulations)

3. Specify domains of analysis using `group_by()`

4. Within `summarize()`, specify variables to calculate, including means, totals, proportions, quantiles, and more

:::

## Descriptive functions {.smaller .bkg-trees}

:::: {.columns}


::: {.column width="50%"}

Use within `summarize()`

- `survey_mean(x)`
- `survey_median(x)`
- `survey_prop()`
- `survey_quantile(x)`
- `survey_ratio(num, den)`
- `survey_sd(x)`
- `survey_total(x)`
- `survey_var(x)`

:::


::: {.column width="50%"}

Common arguments

- `na.rm = FALSE`
- `vartype = c("se", "ci", "var", "cv")`: defaults to just "se"
- `level = 0.95`: confidence level of CIs
- `deff = FALSE`: note can specify as logical OR "replace"
- `df = NULL`: degrees of freedom for CIs (defaults to `degf(design)`)

:::

::::

::: {.notes}
- survey_median/survey_quantile - no deff
- survey_sd - no deff, no measures of variation
- survey_var - no deff, no cv
:::

## Mean examples {.bkg-mountains}

`News`: minutes per day spent on news about politics and current affairs (`nwspol`)

::: {.panel-tabset}

### `na.rm`

```{r}
#| label: 05-mean-na
ess_des |>
  filter(cntry == "IS") |>
  summarize(
    default = survey_mean(News),
    narm = survey_mean(News, na.rm = TRUE)
  )
```

### `vartype`

```{r}
#| label: 05-mean-vartype

ess_des |>
  filter(cntry == "IS") |>
  summarize(
    all = survey_mean(News, na.rm = TRUE, vartype = c("se", "ci", "var", "cv")),
    none = survey_mean(News, na.rm = TRUE, vartype = NULL)
  )
```

### `level` and `df`

```{r}
#| label: 05-mean-ci-options
ess_des |>
  filter(cntry == "IS") |>
  summarize(
    ci95 = survey_mean(News, na.rm = TRUE, vartype = "ci", level = 0.95),
    ci80 = survey_mean(News, na.rm = TRUE, vartype = "ci", level = 0.8),
    ci95_df10 = survey_mean(News, na.rm = TRUE, vartype = "ci", level = 0.95, df = 10)
  )
```


### `deff`

```{r}
#| label: 05-mean-deff

ess_des |>
  filter(cntry == "IS") |>
  summarize(News_mean = survey_mean(News, na.rm = TRUE, deff = "replace"))
```

:::

::: {.notes}
- na.rm removes NA before calculation, similar to many other functions in R
- vartype can choose no option OR multiple
- level and df control confidence intervals
- deff is a design effect, a ratio of the variance under this design compared to a design which is SRS, >1 means less statistically efficient 
:::


## Proportions: motivation {.bkg-mountains .smaller}

And still thinking about different ways of trying to improve things in [country] or help prevent things from going wrong, during the last 12 months, have you done any of the following? Have you volunteered for a not-for-profit or charitable organisation? (`volunfp`)

- 1: Yes
- 2: No
- 7: Refusal*
- 8: Don't know*
- 9: No answer*

Derived variables: `Volunteer_01` (1 = Yes, 0 = No) and `Volunteer_Factor` (factor with levels Yes, No)

::: aside
*Set to missing (`NA`) in the derived variables
:::

## Proportions: two methods {.bkg-mountains .smaller}

Two methods for proportions

1. For binary outcomes, use `survey_mean(x)`
    -  `x` is either 1/0 or TRUE/FALSE
    - can use with `across()` and several outcomes

2. Group the data by the variable (`x`) and then use `survey_prop()`
    - `x` can have 2 or more levels
    - analyzes only one outcome at a time

::: aside
See [Calculating estimates for many outcomes](https://tidy-survey-r.github.io/tidy-survey-book/c05-descriptive-analysis.html#calculating-estimates-for-many-outcomes) for extending to multiple outcomes
:::

## Proportions: two methods, examples {.bkg-mountains}

::: {.panel-tabset}

### `survey_mean()`

```{r}
#| label: 05-np-survey-mean

ess_des |>
  filter(cntry == "SE") |>
  mutate(Volunteer_lgl = as.logical(Volunteer_01)) |>
  summarize(
    across(
      c(Volunteer_lgl, Volunteer_01),
      ~ survey_mean(.x, na.rm = TRUE)
    )
  )
```

### `survey_prop()`

```{r}
#| label: 05-np-survey-prop

ess_des |>
  filter(cntry == "SE", !is.na(Volunteer_Factor)) |>
  group_by(Volunteer_Factor) |>
  summarize(p = survey_prop())
```

:::

::: {.notes}
- survey_mean method only works for binary outcomes, bonus of being able to use across to estimate many outcomes at once
- survey_prop can be used for only one outcome at a time, can work for variables with more than 2 levels
:::

## Proportions: `proportion` argument {.bkg-trees}

`proportion` argument in `survey_mean()`

```{r}
#| label: 05-np-proportion-arg
#| output-location: slide

ess_des |>
  filter(cntry == "SE", !is.na(Volunteer_01)) |>
  summarize(
    p1 = survey_mean(
      Volunteer_01,
      vartype = "ci",
      proportion = FALSE
    ),
    p2 = survey_mean(
      Volunteer_01,
      vartype = "ci",
      proportion = TRUE
    )
  )
```


::: {.notes}
- proportion = TRUE argument only impacts confidence intervals
:::

## Proportions: `prop_method` argument {.bkg-trees}

`prop_method` sets the CI method when `proportion = TRUE` (the default in `survey_prop()`)

```{r}
#| label: 05-np-prop-method-arg
#| eval: false

ess_des |>
  filter(cntry == "SE", !is.na(Volunteer_Factor)) |>
  group_by(Volunteer_Factor) |>
  summarize(
    p1 = survey_prop(vartype = "ci", prop_method = "logit"),
    p2 = survey_prop(vartype = "ci", prop_method = "mean"),
    p3 = survey_prop(vartype = "ci", prop_method = "xlogit")
  )
```

::: aside
Other options include `"likelihood"`, `"asin"`, and `"beta"`. See [`?survey::svyciprop`](https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/survey/refman/survey.html#svyciprop) for details on implementation
:::
## Subgroup analysis

- `filter()` (as in the examples above) subsets the data *after* the design object is created, so standard errors stay correct
- Use `group_by()` to implement domain analysis

## Subgroup analysis: mean and median

- `NetUsage` is 0 if a person uses internet never, only occasionally, or a few times a week; otherwise the reported minutes using internet on a typical day

```{r}
#| label: 05-net-by-country
#| output-location: slide

ess_des |>
  group_by(Country) |>
  summarize(
    Pop = survey_total(vartype = NULL) * 10000,
    NetUse_mean = survey_mean(NetUsage, na.rm = TRUE),
    NetUse_median = survey_median(NetUsage, na.rm = TRUE)
  ) |>
  gt() |>
  fmt_number(columns = starts_with("NetUse"), decimals = 2) |>
  fmt_number(columns = Pop, decimals = 0) |>
  opt_interactive()
```

::: {.notes}
- ESS `pweight` (part of `anweight`) is divided by 10,000, so weighted totals are in units of 10,000 people; multiply by 10,000 to get population estimates (persons aged 15+)
:::

## Crosstabs: marginal {.smaller}

- `NetFreq` is how often people use the internet (categorical)
- `AgeGroup` is a categorical age variable
- With `group_by(AgeGroup, NetFreq)`, proportions sum to 1 *within each age group*

```{r}
#| label: 05-net-freq-age-marg
#| output-location: slide

ess_des |>
  filter(cntry == "FR", !is.na(NetFreq), !is.na(AgeGroup)) |>
  group_by(AgeGroup, NetFreq) |>
  summarize(
    N = survey_total() * 10000,
    p = survey_prop() * 100
  ) |>
  print(n = Inf)
```


## Crosstabs: joint {.smaller}

- `interact()` treats each `AgeGroup` × `NetFreq` combination as one group
- Proportions sum to 1 *across all cells*, not within each age group

```{r}
#| label: 05-net-freq-age-joint
#| output-location: slide

ess_des |>
  filter(cntry == "FR", !is.na(NetFreq), !is.na(AgeGroup)) |>
  group_by(interact(AgeGroup, NetFreq)) |>
  summarize(
    N = survey_total() * 10000,
    p = survey_prop() * 100
  ) |>
  print(n = Inf)
```
